questions.prompt: "Does it scale?" is a meaningful question on its own.
What's the term for how many downstream requests one incoming request causes? (one word, hyphen allowed)
When Twitter moved to pushing each tweet into followers' cached timelines, which load parameter turned out to matter most?
options: The number of tweets posted per second
The distribution of followers per user
The number of data centers serving reads
The average length of a tweet

questions.prompt: After Twitter's switch to fan-out on write, what changed?
options: Writes got cheap and reads got expensive
Reads got cheap and writes got expensive

questions.prompt: Which performance measure matters most for an online service that a person is waiting on?
Strictly speaking, latency is the time a request spends waiting to be handled, while response time is everything the client sees.
You send the same request a thousand times. What should you expect of the response times?
options: Exactly two values: hit and miss
Every run slower than the last
A distribution: most are fast, and some are slow because of GC pauses, lost packets, or cold caches
